reasons: Finding is directionally correct: original § 3.2 imposes a 90-day non-renewal notice window (worse than both the 30-day preferred and 60-day fallback) and renews for a term equal to the prior term, which permits automatic multi-year renewals at the walk-away boundary, with no cap on renewal pricing.

Redline reaches the preferred position on each element: renewal term fixed at twelve (12) months, notice window shortened to thirty (30) days, a 60-day vendor renewal/pricing reminder added, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Failed deterministic check 'non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days (number not found)' is a phrasing artifact — the redline plainly states 'at least thirty (30) days prior' — and the 0.663 changed-character ratio is justified because the rule requires inserting a reminder obligation and an uplift cap that have no counterpart in the original sentence.
Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change and rationale, and offers the 60-day / 5% fallback.

Note for negotiation (not a defect): the notice provision remains mutual, so shortening it to 30 days also lets IBM exit on 30 days' notice; if continuity matters, consider making the 30-day right Customer-only while leaving IBM at 90 days.
